# Identify the point where the Z values for daggers started to increase significantly
# Calculate the cumulative sum of the 'Dagger_inter' column to identify the trend
cumulative_sum = time_series_df['Dagger_inter'].cumsum()

# Find the first CE value where the cumulative sum starts to increase significantly
# This can be done by identifying the first CE where the cumulative sum exceeds a certain threshold
# For simplicity, I will use the mean of the cumulative sum as a threshold
threshold = cumulative_sum.mean()
first_significant_increase = time_series_df[time_series_df['Dagger_inter'].cumsum() > threshold]['CE'].iloc[0]

first_significant_increase

# Calculate the percentage change in the 'Dagger_inter' column over time
time_series_df['Dagger_inter_pct_change'] = time_series_df['Dagger_inter'].pct_change()

# Plot the percentage change to identify when the increase in importance began
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(time_series_df['CE'], time_series_df['Dagger_inter_pct_change'], label='Percentage change in Interpolated Dagger Z values')
plt.xlabel('CE (Common Era)')
plt.ylabel('Percentage change')
plt.title('Percentage change in Interpolated Z values for Daggers over Time')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Identify the first CE value where the percentage change in 'Dagger_inter' becomes statistically significant
# We can use a threshold based on the standard deviation of the percentage change
std_dev = time_series_df['Dagger_inter_pct_change'].std()
threshold = 0.5 * std_dev  # Using half the standard deviation as a threshold for significance

# Find the first CE where the percentage change exceeds the threshold
first_significant_increase = time_series_df[time_series_df['Dagger_inter_pct_change'] > threshold]['CE'].iloc[0]
